note: The repository's mods folder. Jars are dropped into mods/jars/ by hand (they are third-party binaries and git ignores them) and this file describes them, so the launcher can offer the right ones for a version and a mode. tools/launchplan.py reads this, checks every jar is really there, and stages the jars into the deployed site as site/mods/. Only add a mod you are licensed to redistribute.

mods.name: Hello WebMC
mods.note: Built from mods/examples/hello-webmc by tools/build_mods.py. Proves the loader's own mod door: no Minecraft classes, only the loader's API. It has to be built before it can be offered - a jar is never committed.

mods.name: Hello Fabric
mods.note: a Fabric mod built from mods/examples/hello-fabric. On a version with a real JVM it is started by Fabric Loader at play time; on a compiled version the bake applies it before the compile. The one kind of mod that cannot work anywhere is one with native libraries.
